<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|34|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIII.}}</noinclude>and blasphemed against the Holy Ghost (called here the finger of God whereby he wrought miracles) when of malice they attributed the euident workes of God in casting out diuels, to the diuel him self: and this sinne shal not be remitted, because it shal hardly be remitted, as we see by the plague of their posteritie vntil this day.

''32. Nor in the world to come.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Purgatorie.}}S. Augustine and other Holy Doctors gather herevpon, that some sinnes may be remitted in the next life, and consequently prooue Purgatorie thereby. ''De Ciuit. Dei li. 21 c. 13. D. Gregor, Dial. li. 4 c.39''.

''36. Idle word.''] If of euery idle word we must make accoumpt before God in iudgement, and yet shal not for euery such word be damned euerlastingly: then there must needes be some temporal punishment in the next life.

''48. Who is my mother.''] The dutiful affection toward our parents and kinsfolke is not blamed, but the inordinate loue of them to the hinderance of our seruice and duty toward God. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Al Heresies alleage Scriptures.}}Vpon this place some old Heretikes denied Christ to haue any mother. ''Aug. li. de Fid. & Symb. c. 4''. Neither euer was there any heresie so absurd, but it would seeme to haue Scripture for it.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''Speaking in parables (as the Scripture foretold of him, and as meete was for the reprobate Iewes:) he sheweth by the parable of the Sovver, that in the labours of his Church, three partes of foure do perishe through the fault of the hearers. 24 and yet, by the parable of good seede and cockle (as also of the Nette) that his seruants must not for al that, neuer while the vvorld lasteth, make any Schisme or Separation. 31 And by parables of the litle mustardseede and leauen, that notwithstanding the three parts perishing, and ouersowing of cockles, yet that fourth part of the good seede shal spreade ouer al the world. 44 And vvithal, what a treasure, and pearle it is. 53 After al which, yet his owne countrie wil not honour him.''}} {{verse|chapter=13|verse=1}}THE same day {{sc|Iesvs}} going out of the house, sate by the sea side. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=2}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 4, 1. Lu. 8, 4.''}}* great multitudes vvere gathered together vnto him, in so much that he vvent vp into a boate & sate: and al the multitude stoode in the shore, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=3}}† and he spake to them many things in parables, saying,

Behold the sovver vvent forth to sovv. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=4}}† And vvhiles he sovveth, some fell by the vvay side, and the foules of the aire did come and eate it. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=5}}† Othersome also fell vpon rockie places, where they had not much earth: and they shot vp incontinent, because they had not deepenes of earth, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=6}}† and after the sunne vvas vp, they parched: and because they had not roote, they vvithered. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=7}}† And other fell among thornes: and the thornes grevve and choked them. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=8}}† And othersome fell vpon good ground: and they yelded fruite, the {{sup|‖}} one an hundredfold, the other threescore, and an other thirtie. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=9}}† He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=10}}† And his Disciples came and said to him. Why speakest thou to them in parables? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=11}}† Who ansvvered and said vnto them, Because {{sup|‖}} to you it is giuen to knovv the mysteries of the kingdom of heauen: but to them it is not giuen. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=12}}† For<noinclude>{{rh|||he}}</noinclude>
